thread.old_title: The crucifixion as the prophets wrote it — Psalm 22, Isaiah 53, Zechariah 12 and 13, Amos 8, Psalm 69, each in its own words
thread.title: The crucifixion as the prophets wrote it — Psalm 22, Isaiah 53, Zechariah 12 and 13, Amos 8, Psalm 69, each in its own words
thread.old_summary:
It ain't new. Matthew tells the afternoon plainly and keeps pointing at the older scriptures, and the scriptures were already there in detail. The garments:

*And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* (Matthew 27:35)

*They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.* (Psalm 22:18)

The mockery, down to the shaking heads and the taunt about trusting:

*And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads,* (Matthew 27:39)

*All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying,* (Psalm 22:7)

*He trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of Elohim (God).* (Matthew 27:43)

*He trusted on Yahuah (LORD) that he would deliver him: let him deliver him, seeing he delighted in him.* (Psalm 22:8)

The hands and feet:

*For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.* (Psalm 22:16)

The vinegar:

*And straightway one of them ran, and took a spunge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.* (Matthew 27:48)

*They gave me also gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.* (Psalm 69:21)

The darkness at noon, which Amos had set in the day of Yahuah (the LORD):

*Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.* (Matthew 27:45)

*And it shall come to pass in that day, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day:* (Amos 8:9)

Isaiah had written the man himself, despised, silent, wounded for others, buried among the rich:

*He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.* (Isaiah 53:3)

*But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.* (Isaiah 53:5)

*He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.* (Isaiah 53:7)

*And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth.* (Isaiah 53:9)

Zechariah had written the sword against the shepherd and the scattering of the sheep, and who it is that was pierced:

*Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.* (Zechariah 13:7)

*And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.* (Zechariah 12:10)

Mark the speaker in Zechariah. Yahuah (the LORD) says *they shall look upon me whom they have pierced*, and then *they shall mourn for him*. The pierced one is Yahuah (the LORD) in the flesh, and he has a Father; both stand in one verse. The crown of thorns sits beside the oldest curse in the book, read line on line and not as a stated fulfilment:

*And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Yahudim (Jews)!* (Matthew 27:29)

*Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;* (Genesis 3:18)

And the body taken down before night was the Torah kept at the cross:

*His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of Elohim (God);) that thy land be not defiled, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee for an inheritance.* (Deuteronomy 21:23)

Nothing that afternoon was new. Psalm, prophet and Torah had each written their part of it, and Matthew lets the reader see them come together.

cards.src_text: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,
cards.tgt_text: And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.
cards.old_note: *They parted my garments among them ... cast lots upon my vesture* — Tehillim 22:18.
cards.note: Matthew 27:35 — *And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* *And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,* (Matthew 27:33) At the place of the skull the soldiers sit down and divide his clothes by lot, and Matthew says plainly that a prophet had said it first. Psalm 22 has the same men, the same garments and the same lots, written long before anyone stood at Golgotha. The afternoon was not made up as it went.
cards.prose: At the place of the skull the soldiers sit down and divide his clothes by lot, and Matthew says plainly that a prophet had said it first. Psalm 22 has the same men, the same garments and the same lots, written long before anyone stood at Golgotha. The afternoon was not made up as it went.
cards.old_member_note: *They parted my garments among them ... cast lots upon my vesture* — Tehillim 22:18.
cards.member_note: Matthew 27:35 — *which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them.* Matthew names the prophet who had already written the dividing of his clothes at the cross.

cards.old_note: The mocking substance — Tehillim 22:7-8.
cards.note: Matthew 27:39 — *And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads,* *And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,* (Matthew 27:33) The people walking past shake their heads at the man on the cross. Psalm 22 already drew that crowd: onlookers who laugh, curl the lip and shake the head. Matthew only reports what happened on the hill, and the psalm had set it down in advance.

cards.note: Matthew 27:43 — *He trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of Elohim (God).* *And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,* (Matthew 27:33) The taunt throws his trust back in his face: let Elohim (God) rescue him now. Psalm 22 puts nearly the same sneer in the mouths of the onlookers, about trusting Yahuah (LORD) and being delivered. At the skull hill the crowd says out loud what the psalm said they would say.

cards.src_text: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,
cards.tgt_text: And about the ninth hour Yahusha (Jesus) cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My Elohim (God), my Elohim (God), why hast thou forsaken me?
cards.old_note: *Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani* — Tehillim 22:1.
cards.note: Matthew 27:46 — *And about the ninth hour Yahusha (Jesus) cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My Elohim (God), my Elohim (God), why hast thou forsaken me?* *And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,* (Matthew 27:33) Out of the darkness he cries the opening line of Psalm 22, in the speech of the place. The whole psalm stands behind the afternoon: the garments, the mockers, the pierced hands and feet. His cry names the psalm, and the rest of it is being read out in front of the crowd.

cards.tgt_text: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels.

cards.note: Psalm 22:14 — *I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels.* *And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,* (Matthew 27:33) Psalm 22 gives what the body went through: poured out like water, bones pulled apart, the heart melted like wax. cards.tgt_text: And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.

cards.tgt_text: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones.

cards.src_text: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,
cards.tgt_text: Into thine hand I commit my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of truth.

cards.src_text: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,
cards.tgt_text: And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree:
cards.old_note: *He that is hanged is accursed of Elohim.*
cards.note: Deuteronomy 21:22 — *And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree:* *And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,* (Matthew 27:33) This verse names the case: a man put to death and hanged on a tree. The very next line sets the rule that he is buried the same day. Torah already had a place for this hill and a rule for the evening that follows it. Nothing is set aside here. It is kept.

cards.src_text: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,
cards.tgt_text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
cards.old_note: *Thou shalt bruise his heel* — the Cross-bruising substance.
cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* *And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,* (Matthew 27:33) The oldest promise has the woman's seed bruising the serpent's head while his own heel is bruised. At the place of the skull the seed is struck, and the heel is the wound, but it is the head that is crushed. Genesis already had this hill in its first pages.

cards.src_text: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,
cards.tgt_text: And it came to pass after these things, that Elohim (God) did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.
cards.old_note: The Aqedat-Yitschaq Tanakh-typology of the Father offering the Son.
cards.note: Genesis 22:1 — *And it came to pass after these things, that Elohim (God) did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.* *And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,* (Matthew 27:33) Elohim (God) puts Abraham to the test, and Abraham answers with the words *here I am*. The lines after this send him up a mountain with his only son. Golgotha is a Father's Son given up at a hill, and the oldest story already has a father taking his son to the place.

cards.tgt_text: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.
cards.old_note: thread:substantial-crucifixion-tanakh-substances-tehillim-22-and-yeshayahu-53-and-zekharyah-12-10 | *The King silent before Pilate — Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 53:7 walked out, the lamb dumb before her shearers.*
